concepts/envs.title: Environments
concepts/envs.description: An environment owns the scene, robots, observations, and restorable world state. Tasks can reuse one environment with different tools, instructions, and success criteria.

concepts/errors.title: Errors and Recovery
concepts/errors.description: Error injection lets a task expose an agent to temporary execution failures or altered perception. Distinguish an error being available, selected for a stage, and actually triggered on a tool call.

concepts/execution.title: Execution and Concurrency
concepts/execution.description: Three kinds of parallelism are independent: multiple robots in one scene, multiple simulated environments, and multiple models inside an agent system.

concepts/overview.title: Concepts and Architecture
concepts/overview.description: MAGMA separates the interaction an agent must solve from the capabilities used to execute it. A scenario packages reusable components; a task assembles an interaction; stages define how progress is checked.

concepts/perfect-traces.title: Perfect Traces
concepts/perfect-traces.description: A PerfectTrace is a declared reference interaction: user messages, tool calls, expected results, and agent messages. It is not a recorded physics trajectory or proof that a simulated task can be completed.

concepts/requests.title: Requests and Constraints
concepts/requests.description: A request describes one possible interaction event during task construction: an action request, a rule update, a question, or an interruption. It can produce several stages.

concepts/scenarios.title: Scenarios
concepts/scenarios.description: A scenario is a reusable application domain: its environments, task constructors, action capabilities, and optional skills. A Python distribution can provide one or several scenarios.

concepts/stages.title: Stages and Interaction
concepts/stages.description: A stage declares the next checkpoint of an interaction. Tools describe available actions; goals and stage verification determine whether those actions accomplished the objective.

concepts/state.title: State and Observations
concepts/state.description: Use the state owned by the layer you are changing.

concepts/tasks.title: Tasks
concepts/tasks.description: A task is one runnable interaction. It connects an environment, a tools API, an initial situation, and an ordered list of stages.

concepts/tools.title: Tools and Skills
concepts/tools.description: A tool is an elementary capability offered by the scenario. A skill orchestrates tools over time, retaining its own per-call state.

create-scenarios/building-blocks/create-.title: Create an Environment
create-scenarios/building-blocks/create-.description: Create environments in your provider package when an installed environment no longer fits your scenario. The first task can reuse an existing environment; environment authoring is a separate step.

create-scenarios/building-blocks/create-.title: Create a Stage
create-scenarios/building-blocks/create-.description: The first package tutorial defines a complete PressNamedButton stage. Reuse that pattern for a first action checkpoint.

create-scenarios/building-blocks/create-.title: Create a Tool
create-scenarios/building-blocks/create-.description: This example adds a detection tool to your button scenario. It reuses the physical button implementation while explicitly exposing both methods in your concrete API.

create-scenarios/building-blocks/log-ver.title: Verify Execution Logs
create-scenarios/building-blocks/log-ver.description: Use logs when the way an action was performed matters, such as pressing buttons in order or registering a particular attribute. Environment goals answer whether the world is correct; logs preserve execution evidence.

create-scenarios/building-blocks/make-re.title: Make Stages Reusable
create-scenarios/building-blocks/make-re.description: A reusable stage keeps the same verification logic while accepting different objectives and interaction inputs. Parameterize the expected arrangement and checkpoint instead of writing a new class for each task.

create-scenarios/execution/articulated-o.title: Use Articulated Objects
create-scenarios/execution/articulated-o.description: An articulated object exposes more than a rigid actor pose: tools and goals may need joint positions, limits, and machine state. Define that observation contract in your own environment module.

create-scenarios/execution/create-cycle.title: Compose Tools into a Skill
create-scenarios/execution/create-cycle.description: Use a skill when one action should orchestrate several tool calls, inspect intermediate results, and retain progress. The current API replaces the old ToolExecution(..., redo=...) pattern with explicit skill execution.

create-scenarios/execution/env-transitio.title: Change and Preserve Environment State
create-scenarios/execution/env-transitio.description: Choose the mechanism matching the cause of the change.

create-scenarios/execution/errors.title: Inject a Temporary Tool Failure
create-scenarios/execution/errors.description: Begin with one temporary execution error before adding perception or accessibility changes.

create-scenarios/execution/multi-robot.title: Coordinate Robots and Shared Resources
create-scenarios/execution/multi-robot.description: First make each tool work on one robot. Then specify robot identity and how simultaneous calls share resources.

create-scenarios/first-scenario/create-s.title: Create Your Own Scenario Package
create-scenarios/first-scenario/create-s.description: This tutorial creates my_buttons.FirstTask in your own package. It reuses an installed environment and tools, and supplies a custom task and stage. At the end, the scenario is discoverable and its button tool can be exercised interactively.

create-scenarios/first-scenario/create-t.title: Create a Task Preset
create-scenarios/first-scenario/create-t.description: Start from FirstTask in your own package. A preset assembles existing components into an explicit interaction.

create-scenarios/first-scenario/testing.title: Test Your Scenario
create-scenarios/first-scenario/testing.description: If you followed the first tutorial, you have a preset: a task whose stages are already assembled. Follow Check discovery and Test tools in simulation below. That is enough to check the physical button example.

create-scenarios/interactions/asking-req.title: Ask the Agent a Question
create-scenarios/interactions/asking-req.description: Use a text-only stage when success depends on the agent answering a question.

create-scenarios/interactions/constraint.title: Introduce Persistent Rules
create-scenarios/interactions/constraint.description: A persistent rule has a construction-side effect and an interaction-side presentation. Keep those two parts consistent.

create-scenarios/interactions/interrupti.title: Interrupt and Resume an Interaction
create-scenarios/interactions/interrupti.description: Use an interruption when a direct instruction must be handled while a previous action sequence has not yet reached its completion answer.

create-scenarios/interactions/lack-infor.title: Require Clarification from the Agent
create-scenarios/interactions/lack-infor.description: A clarification stage checks whether the agent asks for information it does not have. It is a text-only objective, not a tool that fills in missing data silently.

create-scenarios/interactions/modify-att.title: Modify Task Attributes
create-scenarios/interactions/modify-att.description: Use attribute edits when the agent must add or remove a known value, such as a newly announced delivery location. This changes task vocabulary, not the physical scene.

create-scenarios/interactions/multi-stag.title: Build a Multi-stage Interaction
create-scenarios/interactions/multi-stag.description: One user instruction can require several independently verified actions. Keep the first instruction explicit and subsequent continuation inputs empty.

create-scenarios/overview.title: Create Scenarios and Tasks
create-scenarios/overview.description: Build a first task in your own package, then add only the components and interactions you need.

create-scenarios/procedural-tasks/reques.title: Build Tasks with Requests
create-scenarios/procedural-tasks/reques.description: Once a preset works, use a TaskDefinition to construct varied interactions. This example extends your package and reuses PressNamedButton.

create-scenarios/procedural-tasks/task-r.title: Randomize Public Vocabulary
create-scenarios/procedural-tasks/task-r.description: Vocabulary randomization changes names and descriptions exposed to the model while keeping runtime identifiers stable. It is distinct from physical scene randomization and request sampling.

create-scenarios/traces-and-replay/perfe.title: Add an Optional Perfect Trace
create-scenarios/traces-and-replay/perfe.description: Add a perfect trace only when a consuming workflow needs a declared reference interaction. Ordinary request construction can leave buildperfecttrace unimplemented, returning None through BaseRequest.

create-scenarios/traces-and-replay/seria.title: Make Components Reconstructible
create-scenarios/traces-and-replay/seria.description: Some consumers save task initialization and stage specifications for replay or artifact generation. Execution and serialization are distinct capabilities.

getting-started/installation.description: MAGMA can be installed depending on your needs. We provide 3 installations mode:

getting-started/overview.title: Get Started
getting-started/overview.description: Start by running a provided example before building a scenario or integrating a custom agent system.

intro.title: Welcome to MAGMA
intro.description: MAGMA is a framework for embodied AI agents working on interactive, long-horizon, multi-robot tasks. Use provided scenarios or build your own tasks and environments, generate training data with MAGMA-GEN, and evaluate agents with MAGMA-BENCH.

reference/generation-cli.description: Learn how to launch the generation to adapt MAGMA-GEN to your configuration.

reference/integrations/create-backends.description: Learn how to use your own backends (other than ollama)

reference/overview.title: Reference
reference/overview.description: Look up exact contracts while implementing a scenario in your own provider package.

reference/scenarios/create-stages.title: Stage Contract
reference/scenarios/create-stages.description: Import stage classes and parameter dataclasses from magmacore.simulation.stage; import StageInput and instructions from magmacore.simulation.data_structures.

reference/scenarios/create-tasks.title: Task Preset Contract
reference/scenarios/create-tasks.description: Import BaseTask, InitializationParameters, and TaskMetadata from magma_core.simulation.tasks.

reference/scenarios/create-tasks-definit.title: Task Definitions and Requests
reference/scenarios/create-tasks-definit.description: Import TaskDefinition from magmacore.simulation.tasks, BaseRequest from magmacore.simulation.requests, and TaskState / RuleRenderer from magma_core.simulation.state.

reference/scenarios/create-tools.title: Tool Execution and Result Contract
reference/scenarios/create-tools.description: Import BaseToolsAPI and registertool from magmacore.simulation.tools. Execution data structures are exported from magmacore.simulation.datastructures.

reference/scenarios/errors.title: Error Injection Contract
reference/scenarios/errors.description: BaseError is exported by magmacore.simulation.errors. Declare compatible classes in @registertool(errors=...), optionally wrapped in ToolErrorSupport(error_type, pre=True, post=True).

reference/scenarios/perfect-traces.title: Perfect Trace Contract
reference/scenarios/perfect-traces.description: Core trace events live in magmacore.domain.perfecttrace and are also re-exported from magma_core.simulation.requests.

reference/scenarios/skills.title: Skill Contract
reference/scenarios/skills.description: Import BaseSkill, SkillSpec, SkillTick, CallTick, and MessTick from magma_core.simulation.skills.

reference/templates/requests-template.title: Request Building Blocks
reference/templates/requests-template.description: BaseRequest[ParametersT] lives in magma_core.simulation.requests. Concrete requests must sample parameters and create stages.

reference/templates/stages-template.title: Stage Templates
reference/templates/stages-template.description: Core templates are exported from magma_core.simulation.stage.

use-magma-bench/overview.description: MAGMA-BENCH is the evaluation workflow for testing agents on interactive, long-horizon, multi-robot tasks.

use-magma-gen/coaching-and-generation.description: Learn more about how the generation works and the different components.

use-magma-gen/export.description: Learn how to convert a generated MAGMA-GEN run into training files.

use-magma-gen/overview.title: What can you do with MAGMA-GEN
use-magma-gen/overview.description: MAGMA-GEN is a sophisticated system designed to enable AI agents to perform long-horizon manipulation tasks.
